text.p: Swissair AG said it would invest between 300 million to 400 million Swiss francs in new Airbus A330-200 aircraft.
Swissair has ordered nine A330-200 to replace eight Airbus A310 jets, as part of a joint order with Austrian Airlines and Sabena for 17 Airbus aircraft.
The three carriers have also taken 19 options on the wide-bodied twin-jets, Swissair chief operating officer Philippe Bruggisser said in remarks prepared for a news conference.
Swissair will buy four of the A330s, while five will be leased. Swissair has also acquired options for 10 A330s.
Swissair's fleet of McDonnell Douglas MD11s will be increased to 16 from 13 between now and 1998. A decision to replace five Boeing 747 will be made at a later date.
Separately, Swissair AG, Delta Air Lines Austrian Airlines and Sabena said they will introduce joint operations across the North Atlantic from February 1, 1997, Swissair said.
